Despite the record turnout, isolated incidents of violence were reported across different districts, including clashes between supporters of political parties and attacks on BJP candidates.  The second phase of polling will be held on April 29th.

recent_articles.title: Former DGP R. Sreelekha’s protest slogan sparks debate - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A protest march led by former **Kerala Director General of Police (DGP)** R. Sreelekha in **Thiruvananthapuram** sparked social media debate after she raised slogans deemed derogatory towards the police force. The demonstration, organized by the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Mahila Morcha**, was in response to a clash between BJP and CPI(M) workers at Nettayam and alleged police excesses on BJP activists.

recent_articles.title: West Bengal election - phase 1: 294 candidates face serious criminal charges, 98 booked for crimes against women - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A report by the Association for Democratic Reforms and West Bengal Election Watch revealed that one in five candidates in the first phase of West Bengal Assembly Elections have declared serious criminal cases. The **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** topped the list with 63% of its candidates facing such charges, followed by the **Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI (M)]** and the **All India Trinamool Congress (TMC)**.  The report also highlighted that Nandigram in Purba Medinipur district has six candidates with serious criminal cases, while 66 constituencies are flagged as "red alert" due to multiple candidates facing such charges. The average assets of candidates across the first phase of elections stood at ₹1.34 crore.

recent_articles.title: Kerala fireworks unit blast: CM, Opposition leader express condolences - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan** directed the government to provide timely medical care to victims of a fireworks manufacturing unit fire and explosion in Thrissur, Kerala.  **Mr. Vijayan** expressed condolences for the deaths and stated that expert doctors from outside the state may be called upon if needed. The State Disaster Management department allocated ₹50 lakh to meet emergency needs following the accident.

recent_articles.title: Noida unrest: CPI(M) MP John Brittas raises concern over detentions, due process - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **John Brittas**, a Rajya Sabha member of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), wrote to **Gautam Buddha Nagar Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh** alleging "large-scale illegal detentions" and violations of due process following labor unrest in Noida. The letter cited a joint report by several organizations, including the All India Lawyers Union, Students' Federation of India, and Democratic Youth Federation of India, which alleged that detainees were not provided with copies of FIRs or informed of the grounds of arrest, violating constitutional safeguards. **Mr. Brittas** also raised concerns about the sealing of trade union offices and house arrests of leaders.  The police arrested two more individuals for inciting violence during the protests, while multiple FIRs have been registered under provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act.

recent_articles.title: BJP workers clash with police at Vattiyurkavu - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **BJP** workers clashed with police in Nettayam, Kerala on Sunday evening after a **BJP** worker filed a complaint alleging that his neighbor, an alleged **CPI(M)** activist, had offended his wife. The police intervened after local **CPI(M)** workers challenged the **BJP** worker's accusation, leading to a tense standoff and a baton charge by police.  The **BJP** workers then marched to the Vattiyoorkavu station, accusing the police of siding with the **CPI(M)** activists and targeting media personnel reporting the incident. The situation was eventually brought under control by 11:51 p.m., and increased police patrols have been implemented in the area.

recent_articles.rephrased_article: **V.D. Satheesan**, leader of the Opposition in Kerala, and the **Communist Party of India (Marxist)** have requested an explanation from the **Election Commission of India** regarding the delay in releasing the complete election data for the April 9, 2026, Kerala Assembly elections.
